title: Avro Lancaster W4319
memorial_details: Rectangular, silver-coloured, metal plaque. Bomber Command crest engraved top centre above the dedication. Three crests are engraved below dedication for RNZAF, RAF and RCAF. Dedication is engraved in plain upper and lower-case script.
inscription: Crest: BOMBER COMMAND / ROYAL AIR FORCE / STRIKE HARD STRIKE SURE // Inscription: On the night of 17 December 1942, a Lancaster bomber (coded SR-N; serial no. / W4319) of 101 Squadron, Holme-on-Spalding Moor crashed 200 yards west / of this point. / The aircraft, which was returning from an operation off the North German / coast, was off course and was unable to identify itself because its identification / apparatus (IFF) was not working. The Lancaster crossed the coast just north of / Redcar during an attack on the Tees area. In the absence of IFF, a Bofors anti- / aircraft gun crew based at Warrenby Works assumed that the Lancaster was a / raider and shot it down. / There were no survivors amongst the crew of seven. / (7 Names) / LEST WE FORGET // Three service crests, left to right: { ROYAL NEW ZEALAND AIR FORCE / PER ARDUA AD ASTRA } { PER ARDUA AD ASTRA } { PER ARDUA AD ASTRA / ROYAL CANADIAN AIR FORCE }
